messages:
maria-gonzalez: Heads up — we're starting onboarding for HaloX-14B (v1.0) for the recommendation experiments. Found some weird license language, can legal eyes weigh in?

kevin-cho: dropping the snippet from the repo where the weights were published:
```
License: MIT + NonCommercial-Subset
Clause: Redistribution of derivative models permitted for research and internal production, but commercial hosted APIs require explicit permission. Attribution required: 'HaloX authors' and link.
Export: No embargo noted.
```

sara_t: tl;dr — sounds like mixed permissive + noncommercial. That could block our hosted API offering, but Dedicated/private might be ok depending on interpretation.

ajones: if "internal production" is allowed, Dedicated + Private would be fine. Hosted API is probably a no-go unless we get written permission. We should confirm whether the "commercial hosted APIs" phrase means any payer-facing API or just third-party marketplaces.

maria-gonzalez: Good point. Our inference product has three surfaces (hosted, dedicated, private). We need a clean rubric: can we run evals, quantize and publish benchmarks publicly, and ship quantized weights to Dedicated customers?

legal-bot: Looping in legal ops. Quick checklist from legal: 1) Is the canonical upstream license a single-file artifact or combined with a contributor agreement? 2) Are weights distributed under the same license or S3 terms? 3) Any additional readme or privacy/data use terms?

kevin-cho: Answers: 1) single LICENSE.md in repo, 2) weights have separate agreement text in the release notes (not linked to LICENSE.md), 3) release notes include a line: "By downloading weights you accept that you will not operate a commercial hosted API without permission."

sara_t: Ok — commercially-hosted APIs explicitly blocked without permission. For our onboarding runbook: we can run evals and internal latency/cost quant experiments. We should avoid publishing downloadable quantized weights publicly and avoid including the model on our hosted catalog.

maria-gonzalez: If we restrict to internal eval and Dedicated/private channels, do we still need attribution when we surface benchmark numbers or evaluation artifacts? The license had an "attribution required" line.

legal-bot: Attribution requirement typically applies to derivative distributions and published artifacts that include model outputs or weights. For benchmark numbers and papers, standard practice is to include an attribution note like: 'Model: HaloX-14B (HaloX authors), used under license; see link.' That should satisfy attribution. Avoid repackaging weights without permission.

ajones: Questions on quantization: If we run 4-bit PTQ for internal performance profiling and then share quantization parameters with a Dedicated customer as part of deployment, is that "distribution of derivative weights"?

legal-bot: Likely yes. If quantized weights are materially different artifacts delivered to customers, that counts as distribution of derivatives. We need explicit permission in the license or a granted exception. Consider a narrow workaround: provide a deployment container that performs quantization at customer site within their VPC (so we don't hand over derived binaries).

kevin-cho: Implementation note: we can add a step to the onboarding runbook — for models with ambiguous redistribution terms, avoid exporting derived binaries. Instead, create a private operator image that fetches and quantizes weights on first boot in-customer.

maria-gonzalez: For evals we also run bias/regression suites and plan to publish eval dashboards internally. Any guardrails for which prompts/sensitive datasets we can include?

legal-bot: Don't publish prompts or dataset excerpts containing third-party personal data. For sensitive-regulated domains, sanitize or use synthetic prompts. Tag any public-facing metric with 'evaluation performed under license restrictions — no weights redistributed'.

sara_t: Sounds like the runbook action items: 1) mark HaloX-14B 'hosted-prohibited' until permission cleared, 2) allow internal eval and Dedicated/private deploy via in-customer quantization, 3) add mandatory attribution text for published benchmarks, 4) ask upstream for explicit commercial hosted permission (email template needed).

ajones: I'll add a checklist PR to model-onboarding repo and prototype the 'on-site quantize' container pattern.

maria-gonzalez: Can legal-bot (or someone from legal ops) draft the email template and confirm whether upstream maintainer is open to granting hosted API rights for enterprise customers?

legal-bot: Will draft. Also suggest we capture the release-note snippet into our license-tracking sheet with a flag 'requires upstream consent for hosted'.

kevin-cho: One more operational thing — telemetry. We'll need a telemetry opt-in for Dedicated customers if we run on-site quantization to collect perf numbers (and that has to be documented in the contract).

maria-gonzalez: Great. Thanks all — moving to action items. I'll update the onboarding PR and tag legal for the template. :thumbsup:
